topic.title: Language-Model Mechanisms and Systematic Generalization
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: This topic investigates what computations language models learn and how those computations transfer beyond familiar examples. Papers study depth, emergent abilities, in-context learning, length generalization, grammar structure, and the reversibility of interventions. One representative analysis deletes or swaps layers and uses differing sensitivity across depth to motivate hypotheses about stages of inference.
topic.whyItMatters: Strong task performance does not uniquely identify the mechanism producing it. Controlled interventions and simplified formal languages can test explanations and reveal why a model generalizes along some dimensions while failing along others.
topic.evolution: Early representatives concern language learning and role binding. Later work examines reasoning and pretrained-transformer behavior. Recent studies combine structural interventions, concept ablation, and grammar-based theory; analyses of subgrammars distinguish learning dynamics and internal alignment from improvements in final predictive performance.
openQuestions: Which mechanistic hypotheses make predictions that distinguish them from alternatives?
How well do findings from controlled grammars explain generalization in natural language and code?

papers.title: Representative Language Generation
papers.tldr: A theoretical framework defines proportionally representative generation and establishes conditional feasibility alongside computational limits.

papers.title: Roll the dice & look before you leap: Going beyond the creative limits of next-token prediction
papers.tldr: Controlled creativity tasks favor multi-token learning and show that input noise can rival temperature sampling for coherent diversity.

papers.title: Scaling Sparse Feature Circuits For Studying In-Context Learning
papers.tldr: Sparse feature circuits reveal causally connected task-detection and task-execution features involved in in-context learning.

papers.title: Sparsing Law: Towards Large Language Models with Greater Activation Sparsity
papers.tldr: A quantitative study of activation sparsity guides a 2.4-billion-parameter model with 93.52% sparsity and a 4.1-fold speedup over its dense version.

papers.title: SPEX: Scaling Feature Interaction Explanations for LLMs
papers.tldr: SPEX uses sparse interaction structure to scale model-agnostic explanations to roughly 1,000 input features.

papers.title: The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence
papers.tldr: Refusal involves multiple independent directions and concept cones, and geometric orthogonality alone does not establish independence under intervention.

papers.title: The Missing Alignment Link of In-context Learning on Sequences
papers.tldr: ICA-Tune improves studied sequence-to-sequence learning by encouraging input-output alignment and more complete induction heads.

papers.title: The Role of Sparsity for Length Generalization in LLMs
papers.tldr: Sparse token dependencies provide a theoretical route to length generalization and motivate a learned extension of position coupling.

papers.title: To Steer or Not to Steer? Mechanistic Error Reduction with Abstention for Language Models
papers.tldr: MERA calibrates when and how to steer language-model activations, improving performance or abstaining when no confident correction is available.

papers.title: Towards Global-level Mechanistic Interpretability: A Perspective of Modular Circuits of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: ModCirc discovers reusable, interpreted computational modules to connect language-model explanations across tasks and reduce repeated interpretation work.

papers.title: Understanding Multimodal LLMs Under Distribution Shifts: An Information-Theoretic Approach
papers.tldr: An information-theoretic framework bounds changes in multimodal query-response relevance using visual and textual distribution discrepancies.

papers.title: Unnatural Languages Are Not Bugs but Features for LLMs
papers.tldr: The study finds transferable semantic features in human-unreadable text and comparable instruction-tuning performance using unnatural-language datasets.

papers.title: When do neural networks learn world models?
papers.tldr: The paper proves latent-variable recovery in a multi-task setting for models with a low-degree bias under stated assumptions, with results sensitive to architecture.

papers.title: Which Attention Heads Matter for In-Context Learning?
papers.tldr: Ablations across 12 language models identify function-vector heads as the main drivers of few-shot in-context learning, especially in larger models.

papers.title: A Compressive-Expressive Communication Framework for Compositional Representations
papers.tldr: CELEBI combines three communication pressures to help artificial agents learn compact, expressive, and more compositional messages.

papers.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.tldr: Sparse autoencoders can hide broad concepts inside narrower features, undermining the reliability of apparently interpretable features.

papers.title: Absence Bench: Language Models Can’t See What’s Missing
papers.tldr: AbsenceBench reveals that language models can struggle to identify deleted information even when given both original and edited documents.

papers.title: Attention Sinks: A 'Catch, Tag, Release' Mechanism for Embeddings
papers.tldr: Attention sinks can organize token representations by assigning meaningful shared tags that later computation uses to retrieve them.

papers.title: Benford’s Curse: Tracing Digit Bias to Numerical Hallucination in LLMs
papers.tldr: The paper links biased numerical generation to a small set of digit-selective neurons and shows that pruning them partially corrects numerical errors.

papers.title: Brain-Informed Fine-Tuning for Improved Multilingual Understanding in Language Models
papers.tldr: Fine-tuning language models with bilingual brain recordings improves brain encoding and most evaluated language tasks across multiple languages.

papers.title: Brain-tuning Improves Generalizability and Efficiency of Brain Alignment in Speech Models
papers.tldr: Training speech models jointly on multiple participants' brain responses improves brain alignment, data efficiency, and semantic task performance.

papers.title: CALM: Culturally Self-Aware Language Models
papers.tldr: CALM organizes and adaptively combines cultural signals, then uses reflective learning to improve culturally sensitive language-model behavior.

papers.title: Causal Head Gating: A Framework for Interpreting Roles of Attention Heads in Transformers
papers.tldr: CHG learns attention-head gates to identify causal task roles, revealing sparse sufficient circuits and interaction-dependent head behavior.

papers.title: Concept-Guided Interpretability via Neural Chunking
papers.tldr: Neural chunking extracts recurring concept-related activity patterns, and inducing those patterns changes the concepts networks generate.

papers.title: Correlation Dimension of Autoregressive Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Correlation dimension measures recurring structure in model-perceived text complexity and empirically reveals training phases, hallucination tendencies, and generation degeneration.

papers.title: Counterfactual reasoning: an analysis of in-context emergence
papers.tldr: Controlled tasks show Transformers can perform in-context counterfactual reasoning by recovering latent concepts and carrying factual noise into hypothetical predictions.

papers.title: Dense SAE Latents Are Features, Not Bugs
papers.tldr: Frequently active sparse-autoencoder features often capture meaningful language-model computations rather than training noise.

papers.title: Detoxifying Large Language Models via Autoregressive Reward Guided Representation Editing
papers.tldr: ARGRE learns toxicity transitions in internal representations to guide faster, more effective test-time detoxification across eight evaluated language models.

papers.title: DISCO: Disentangled Communication Steering for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: DISCO steers attention queries and values directly, enabling finer control and higher measured steering efficacy than compared baselines.

papers.title: Do Language Models Use Their Depth Efficiently?
papers.tldr: Analyses of three model families suggest extra depth often spreads similar computations across more layers instead of introducing new kinds of computation.

papers.title: Dynamics of Spontaneous Topic Changes in Next Token Prediction with Self-Attention
papers.tldr: Theory and experiments identify constraints on spontaneous topic changes in self-attention models that differ from patterns of human thought.

papers.title: Emergence of Linear Truth Encodings in Language Models
papers.tldr: A toy transformer shows how truth-related co-occurrence patterns can make linear truth representations emerge through next-token learning.

papers.title: Exploring the Translation Mechanism of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Causal interventions identify a sparse translation mechanism, and targeted fine-tuning of less than 5% of parameters improves translation in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Extrapolation by Association: Length Generalization Transfer In Transformers
papers.tldr: Transformers can transfer length generalization from longer related tasks, with initial evidence linking transfer to shared attention heads.

papers.title: Failure by Interference: Language Models Make Balanced Parentheses Errors When Faulty Mechanisms Overshadow Sound Ones
papers.tldr: RASteer improves syntactic and arithmetic performance by strengthening reliable model components that can otherwise be overshadowed by faulty ones.

papers.title: FALCON: Fine-grained Activation Manipulation by Contrastive Orthogonal Unalignment for Large Language Model
papers.tldr: FALCON guides unlearning through representations and orthogonal gradient projections, improving forgetting while preserving utility in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Far from the Shallow: Brain-Predictive Reasoning Embedding through Residual Disentanglement
papers.tldr: Separating linguistic features from model embeddings reveals reasoning-related brain activity with distinct predictive and temporal properties.

papers.title: Flexible Language Modeling in Continuous Space with Transformer-based Autoregressive Flows
papers.tldr: Transformer-based autoregressive flows model language in continuous space, supporting bidirectional context, flexible generation blocks, and hierarchical decoding passes.

papers.title: Generalization or Hallucination? Understanding Out-of-Context Reasoning in Transformers
papers.tldr: The paper links useful generalization and hallucination to a shared association mechanism, with a theoretical explanation in a simplified transformer.

papers.title: Geometry of Decision Making in Language Models
papers.tldr: A study of 28 language models finds that representation dimension expands in middle layers and contracts toward decision-relevant structure in later layers.

papers.title: HELM: Hyperbolic Large Language Models via Mixture-of-Curvature Experts
papers.tldr: HELM scales fully hyperbolic language models to billions of parameters, reporting gains in reasoning benchmarks and semantic hierarchy modeling.

papers.title: Hierarchical Frequency Tagging Probe (HFTP): A Unified Approach to Investigate Syntactic Structure Representations in Large Language Models and the Human Brain
papers.tldr: HFTP probes syntactic representations in language models and the brain, finding that model upgrades do not uniformly increase brain similarity.

papers.title: InfiGFusion: Graph-on-Logits Distillation via Efficient Gromov-Wasserstein for Model Fusion
papers.tldr: InfiGFusion improves language-model fusion by distilling token co-activation graphs with an efficient, theoretically supported structural comparison.

papers.title: Interpretable Next-token Prediction via the Generalized Induction Head
papers.tldr: GIM combines exact and learned sequence matching to improve interpretable language prediction and fMRI response prediction.

papers.title: L$^2$M: Mutual Information Scaling Law for Long-Context Language Modeling
papers.tldr: L²M uses a mutual-information scaling law to derive a necessary lower bound on the history-state capacity required for effective long-context modeling.

papers.title: Language Model Behavioral Phases are Consistent Across Architecture, Training Data, and Scale
papers.tldr: Across the studied architectures, datasets, and scales, language models exhibit similar pretraining phases largely explained by three word-level heuristics.

papers.title: Language Models Are Capable of Metacognitive Monitoring and Control of Their Internal Activations
papers.tldr: A neurofeedback-style experiment measures language models’ limited ability to report and control their activations.

papers.title: Learning the Wrong Lessons: Syntactic-Domain Spurious Correlations in Language Models
papers.tldr: Language models can learn misleading associations between grammatical patterns and subject areas that impair instruction interpretation and sometimes enable refusal bypasses.

papers.title: Less is More: Local Intrinsic Dimensions of Contextual Language Models
papers.tldr: Changes in local embedding dimension provide empirical signals of training behavior, with decreases tending to precede performance gains.

papers.title: LLM Layers Immediately Correct Each Other
papers.tldr: Adjacent transformer layers often selectively counteract each other's updates, complicating interpretations that treat features as simply accumulating.

papers.title: Measuring and Guiding Monosemanticity
papers.tldr: The paper introduces a monosemanticity metric and concept-guided sparse autoencoders that improve feature isolation and fine-grained model steering.

papers.title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures
papers.tldr: Nested Learning treats models and optimizers as interacting learning processes, motivating new optimizers, self-modifying sequence models, and continuum memory.

papers.title: On the Entropy Calibration of Language Models
papers.tldr: Entropy miscalibration improves slowly with scale, but reducing entropy without worsening log loss is theoretically possible under a future-entropy prediction assumption.

papers.title: Overcoming Sparsity Artifacts in Crosscoders to Interpret Chat-Tuning
papers.tldr: Latent Scaling and BatchTopK training reduce crosscoder artifacts, enabling more reliable identification of concepts associated with chat-tuning.

papers.title: PaceLLM: Brain-Inspired Large Language Models for Long-Context Understanding
papers.tldr: PaceLLM combines persistent activation memory with semantic grouping of feed-forward weights to improve long-context understanding.

papers.title: ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.tldr: ParamMute suppresses feed-forward networks associated with unfaithful answers to help language models follow accurate retrieved evidence.

papers.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 4.1, Architecture Design and the Magic of Canon Layers
papers.tldr: Controlled synthetic tasks reveal that lightweight Canon layers improve several language-model capabilities by mixing information across neighboring tokens.

papers.title: Pre-trained Large Language Models Learn to Predict Hidden Markov Models In-context
papers.tldr: Pretrained language models learn to predict Hidden Markov Model sequences from context and show competitive results on animal decision-making data.

papers.title: Remarkable Robustness of LLMs: Stages of Inference?
papers.tldr: Layer deletion and swapping reveal uneven sensitivity across language model depth, motivating a four-stage hypothesis of inference.

papers.title: Scaling and context steer LLMs along the same computational path as the human brain
papers.tldr: Language-model layers align with successive brain responses in a similar order, with the pattern depending on model size and context length.

papers.title: Self-Verification Provably Prevents Model Collapse in Recursive Synthetic Training
papers.tldr: The paper derives conditions under which confidence-based self-verification prevents model collapse even when recursive training uses only synthetic data.

papers.title: SPACE: Noise Contrastive Estimation Stabilizes Self-Play Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: SPACE uses noise contrastive estimation to stabilize self-play fine-tuning and improve learning from limited real data.

papers.title: Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling
papers.tldr: The paper links strong representation superposition to inverse-dimension loss scaling across a broad class of feature-frequency distributions.

papers.title: Task-Specific Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Monosemantic Neuronal Activations
papers.tldr: The method selects instruction-tuning examples using sparse, disentangled model activations, improving selection stability and target-task performance in the reported experiments.

papers.title: The Emergence of Abstract Thought in Large Language Models Beyond Any Language
papers.tldr: The authors identify a small, increasingly important multilingual parameter core and use its properties to motivate neuron-specific training strategies.

papers.title: The emergence of sparse attention: impact of data distribution and benefits of repetition
papers.tldr: Theory and small-Transformer experiments explain sparse attention emergence, showing power-law timing and substantial acceleration from repetition.

papers.title: TinyTim: a family of language models for divergent generation
papers.tldr: TinyTim models fine-tuned on Finnegans Wake exhibit persistent lexical invention, with instruction tuning preserving that style at a cost to benchmark performance.

papers.title: Token Embeddings Violate the Manifold Hypothesis
papers.tldr: A statistical test finds frequent local irregularities in token embeddings, challenging manifold assumptions and suggesting reduced stability for prompts containing implicated tokens.

papers.title: Towards Interpretability Without Sacrifice: Faithful Dense Layer Decomposition with Mixture of Decoders
papers.tldr: Mixture of Decoders uses sparse, expressive sublayers to improve the accuracy of interpretable language-model layer decompositions.

papers.title: Tracing the Representation Geometry of Language Models from Pretraining to Post-training
papers.tldr: Representation geometry reveals three pretraining phases and distinct post-training tradeoffs involving performance, robustness, reward alignment, and diversity.

papers.title: Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching
papers.tldr: Affine mappings transfer features and sparse-autoencoder weights between language models, with transferred initialization enabling 50% cheaper autoencoder training in a reported example.

papers.title: Understanding LLM Behaviors via Compression: Data Generation, Knowledge Acquisition and Scaling Laws
papers.tldr: A compression-based theory connects language-model scaling, knowledge acquisition, and hallucinations through a simplified hierarchical data model.

papers.title: Unifying Attention Heads and Task Vectors via Hidden State Geometry in In-Context Learning
papers.tldr: The paper links attention heads and task vectors through a two-stage pattern of early separability and later alignment in classification representations.

papers.title: Vision-and-Language Training Helps Deploy Taxonomic Knowledge but Does Not Fundamentally Alter It
papers.tldr: Vision-language training often improves taxonomic question answering by helping models use existing knowledge, without substantially changing that knowledge.

papers.title: Wisdom is Knowing What not to Say: Hallucination-Free LLMs Unlearning via Attention Shifting
papers.tldr: Attention-Shifting selectively suppresses unwanted knowledge while reinforcing retained information to improve the balance between unlearning and reliable responses.

papers.title: A geometric relation of the error introduced by sampling a language model’s output distribution to its internal state
papers.tldr: A geometric analysis of token embeddings links sampling sensitivity to meaningful internal structure on chess reasoning tasks.

papers.title: A Narrowing Geometry in Contaminated Reasoning
papers.tldr: The paper links contaminated reasoning to increasingly concentrated internal representations and uses that analysis to help restore base-model reasoning behavior.

papers.title: Abstraction Induces the Brain Alignment of Language and Speech Models
papers.tldr: The study links models’ ability to predict brain responses to rich meaning representations and high intrinsic dimension in intermediate layers.

papers.title: All Circuits Lead to Rome: Rethinking Functional Anisotropy in Circuit and Sheaf Discovery for LLMs
papers.tldr: Multiple structurally different circuits can explain the same LLM behavior, challenging the assumption that discovered mechanisms are nearly unique.

papers.title: An Information-Theoretic Criterion for Efficient Data Synthesis
papers.tldr: The paper argues that useful synthetic-data learning requires external task information and depends on which supervision signals are easiest to learn.

papers.title: Belief Dynamics Reveal the Dual Nature of In-Context Learning and Activation Steering
papers.tldr: A Bayesian model explains and predicts prompt-based and activation-based control as changes to evidence and concept priors.

papers.title: BLOCK-EM: Preventing Emergent Misalignment via Latent Blocking
papers.tldr: Constraining selected internal features substantially reduces emergent misalignment in tested settings, although extended fine-tuning can weaken the protection.

papers.title: Breaking the Reversal Curse in Autoregressive Language Models via Identity Bridge
papers.tldr: Adding identity statements to training data helps language models learn reverse relations, challenging the claim that the reversal curse is unavoidable.

papers.title: Bridging the Knowledge-Prediction Gap in LLMs on Multiple-Choice Questions
papers.tldr: KAPPA aligns internal knowledge and prediction subspaces to help language models use answers they already encode.

papers.title: C$^2$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.tldr: A cross-sample regularizer makes sparse autoencoder features more consistent while preserving reconstruction fidelity.

papers.title: Capacity without Access: Reinterpreting the Mid-Depth Spectral Plateau in LLMs
papers.tldr: The analyzed intermediate LLM layers retain rich representations, but geometric misalignment limits their access to the final prediction.

papers.title: Causes and Consequences of Representational Similarity in Machine Learning Models
papers.tldr: Dataset and task overlap are associated with greater model-representation similarity, which also correlates with adversarial attack transfer in vision models.

papers.title: Chiral Symmetry Breaking in Transformers: A Group-Equivariant Framework for Addressing the Reversal Curse via Adjoint Manifold Mappings
papers.tldr: A learned symmetry-aware mapping improves inverse-fact retrieval, supporting a representation-access explanation for part of the reversal curse.

papers.title: Cognitive Fatigue in Autoregressive Transformers: Formalization and Measurement
papers.tldr: The Fatigue Index combines three internal signals to track and predict degradation during long language-model generations in the evaluated models.

papers.title: Concept Heterogeneity-aware Representation Steering
papers.tldr: CHaRS steers language models with input-dependent combinations of cluster-level shifts instead of one global direction.

papers.title: Context-level Language Modeling by Learning Predictive Context Embeddings
papers.tldr: ContextLM improves language-model efficiency by adding prediction of multi-token context embeddings to standard pretraining.

papers.title: DecodeShare: Tracing the Shared Subspace of LLM Decode-Time Decisions
papers.tldr: DecodeShare identifies a compact, shared decoding subspace whose removal strongly disrupts decisions and whose overlap matters for activation steering.

papers.title: Deep sequence models tend to memorize geometrically; it is unclear why
papers.tldr: Sequence models can organize facts into global embedding geometries that simplify reasoning, with a Node2Vec connection revealing a possible underlying spectral bias.

papers.title: Demystifying When Pruning Works via Representation Hierarchies
papers.tldr: Pruning can preserve hidden representations while amplifying probability errors that persist during generation, helping explain its uneven effects across tasks.

papers.title: Deriving Neural Scaling Laws from the Statistics of Natural Language
papers.tldr: The paper predicts data-limited scaling exponents from token-correlation decay and context-dependent uncertainty, closely matching experiments on TinyStories and WikiText.

papers.title: Detecting the Semantic Fixed Point: A Geometric Framework for Efficient Inference
papers.tldr: Tracking when hidden-state updates become small and aligned enables early exits that save 30–35% of FLOPs while retaining over 98% of full-depth accuracy in the reported tests.

papers.title: Differential syntactic and semantic encoding in LLMs
papers.tldr: Sentence-vector averages reveal partially separable, partly linear encodings of syntax and meaning in DeepSeek-V3.

papers.title: Diffusion Models Preferentially Memorize Prototypical Examples or: Why Does My Diffusion Model Love Slop?
papers.tldr: In structured-string experiments, diffusion models memorize common patterns first, while greater high-level diversity delays memorization.

papers.title: Dispersion Loss Counteracts Embedding Condensation and Improves Generalization in Small Language Models
papers.tldr: A training loss that spreads token embeddings improves small language models across ten benchmarks without adding parameters.

papers.title: DLM-Scope: Mechanistic Interpretability of Diffusion Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
papers.tldr: DLM-Scope extracts interpretable diffusion-language-model features that support steering, decoding analysis, and sometimes lower early-layer loss.

papers.title: Do Activation Verbalization Methods Convey Privileged Information?
papers.tldr: Existing activation-verbalization evaluations can reward descriptions that reflect inputs or the verbalizer’s knowledge rather than target-model internals.

papers.title: Do Language Models Track Entities Across State Changes?
papers.tldr: The studied language models track changing entities through parallel information aggregation, with a fragile removal mechanism that predicts observable failures.

papers.title: Do LLMs "Feel"? Emotion Circuits Discovery and Control
papers.tldr: The study identifies and causally tests language-model emotion circuits, then uses them to control emotional expression with high test-set accuracy.

papers.title: Do LLMs Signal When They’re Right? Evidence from Neuron Agreement
papers.tldr: Neuron Agreement Decoding uses sparse, consistent internal activations to select promising answers and stop weak generations early.

papers.title: Domain Restriction via Multi SAE Layer Transitions
papers.tldr: Sparse-autoencoder representations of changes between language-model layers provide useful signatures for detecting out-of-domain inputs.

papers.title: Dual Mechanisms of Value Expression: Intrinsic vs. Prompted Values in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Intrinsic and prompted value expression share some internal components but also engage mechanisms with different behavioral roles.

papers.title: Endogenous Resistance to Activation Steering in Language Models
papers.tldr: Some language models recover from task-conflicting activation steering, and the paper identifies internal signals and interventions associated with this resistance.

papers.title: Facts in Stats: Impacts of Pretraining Diversity on Language Model Generalization
papers.tldr: A synthetic pretraining testbed shows that contextual diversity trades off learning speed and generalization, with the best level depending on training budget.

papers.title: FedSDR: Federated Self-Distillation with Rectification
papers.tldr: FedSDR combines local self-distillation with a raw-data rectification branch to address federated data differences while protecting factual fidelity.

papers.title: Fine-grained Analysis of Brain-LLM Alignment through Input Attribution
papers.tldr: Word-level attribution shows that brain alignment and next-word prediction rely on largely different input information.

papers.title: From Associations to Activations: Comparing Behavioral and Hidden-State Semantic Geometry in LLMs
papers.tldr: Forced-choice word judgments reveal more about language models' hidden semantic geometry than free association does.

papers.title: Geometry of Reason: Spectral Signatures of Valid Mathematical Reasoning
papers.tldr: Training-free spectral measurements of attention distinguish valid mathematical reasoning and improve proof selection, with the most useful measurement depending on architecture.

papers.title: How Do Language Models Speak Languages? A Case Study on Unintended Code-Switching
papers.tldr: The study links unintended language switching to competition between semantic and language-maintenance circuits, then reduces switching through a small targeted update.

papers.title: How does Chain of Thought decompose complex tasks?
papers.tldr: A classification-tree model of chain of thought identifies when decomposition helps and why increasing reasoning depth eventually stops improving error.

papers.title: How Does the Pretraining Distribution Shape In-Context Learning? A Fundamental Trade-Off
papers.tldr: The paper identifies a trade-off in which heavy-tailed pretraining distributions improve robust task selection but hinder generalization, especially with little data.

papers.title: How Language Models Process Negation
papers.tldr: The studied models internally process negation through suppression and constructive representations, but late-layer shortcuts can override that capability.

papers.title: How Transformers Represent Hierarchies: A Local-to-Global Mechanism
papers.tldr: In a controlled grammar setting, Transformers build local patterns into global parsing representations that support next-token prediction.

papers.title: Introspection Adapters: Training LLMs to Report Their Learned Behaviors
papers.tldr: Adapters trained on deliberately implanted behaviors help language models describe learned behaviors and support audits of misaligned models.

papers.title: Inverse Depth Scaling From Most Layers Being Similar
papers.tldr: The paper finds inverse-depth loss scaling and proposes that similar layers may improve predictions through averaging rather than compositional computation.

papers.title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models
papers.tldr: Layerwise analysis reveals redundant computation in tabular foundation models and motivates a looped single-layer prototype with 20% of the original parameters.

papers.title: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
papers.tldr: The authors trace sparse, causally effective language-model circuits directly through MLP neurons without training an additional feature decomposition.

papers.title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
papers.tldr: Diffusion models trained on LLM activations learn useful priors for fluent steering and increasingly isolate concepts as training loss improves.

papers.title: Linguistic Properties and Model Scale in Brain Encoding: From Small to Compressed Language Models
papers.tldr: In the studied models, 3-billion-parameter models match larger models in predicting brain activity, and most compression methods preserve that ability despite weakening linguistic performance.

papers.title: Logit Distance Bounds Representational Similarity
papers.tldr: A logit-based distance provides guarantees and empirical benefits for preserving linear representational structure during model distillation.

papers.title: Masks Can Be Distracting: On Context Comprehension in Diffusion Language Models
papers.tldr: Generation masks can distract diffusion language models from context, and a mask-agnostic fine-tuning loss substantially reduces this effect.

papers.title: Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing the Training Origins of Interpretable LLM Units
papers.tldr: Mechanistic Data Attribution identifies training samples whose targeted modification causally changes interpretable heads and associated in-context learning behavior.

papers.title: MEG-XL: Data-Efficient Brain-to-Text via Long-Context Pre-Training
papers.tldr: MEG-XL uses minutes of neural context during pretraining to improve word decoding with substantially less fine-tuning data.

papers.title: MidSteer: Optimal Affine Framework for Steering Generative Models
papers.tldr: MidSteer develops affine concept steering with minimal disturbance, extending a theory linking behavior removal, concept erasure, and concept switching.

papers.title: Multilingual Unlearning in LLMs: Transfer, Dynamics, and Reversibility
papers.tldr: Multilingual tests find uneven unlearning transfer and substantial reversibility, suggesting that the studied methods often suppress rather than erase knowledge.

papers.title: Not All Answers Are Contextually Persuadable: Inference Dynamics in Large Language Models under Contextual Influence
papers.tldr: Repeated contextual assertions drive predictions toward query-dependent stable regimes, so repetition may either fail to change an answer or make change inevitable.

papers.title: Old Habits Die Hard: How Conversational History Geometrically Traps LLMs
papers.tldr: History Echoes links persistent conversational behavior to geometric confinement in language models’ hidden representations.

papers.title: Patterning: The Dual of Interpretability
papers.tldr: Patterning inverts a mathematical response relationship to choose training-data changes that steer a model’s internal structures and learned algorithms.

papers.title: PolySAE: Modeling Feature Interactions in Sparse Autoencoders via Polynomial Decoding
papers.tldr: PolySAE adds efficient polynomial feature interactions to sparse autoencoders, improving semantic probing and enabling causal steering toward compositional meanings.

papers.title: PonderLM-2: Pretraining LLM with Latent Thoughts in Continuous Space
papers.tldr: PonderLM-2 pretrains models to perform latent thought steps before each token, outperforming a twice-larger standard model at matched inference cost.

papers.title: Position: Prioritize Identifying Structure, Not Complex Models, for Scientific Discovery
papers.tldr: Accurate predictions and persuasive explanations do not establish a mechanism when incompatible mechanisms fit the same observations.

papers.title: Predicting the Emergence of Induction Heads in Language Model Pretraining
papers.tldr: Batch and context size predict induction-head emergence, while repeated-bigram frequency and reliability strongly influence whether heads form.

papers.title: Prototype Transformer: Towards Language Model Architectures Interpretable by Design
papers.tldr: ProtoT replaces self-attention with efficient prototype channels that learn nameable concepts, offering potential for more interpretable language models.

papers.title: Random Scaling of Emergent Capabilities
papers.tldr: Apparent capability breakthroughs can arise from changing probabilities of training outcomes across random seeds as models scale.

papers.title: Regret Pre-training: Bridging Prior and Posterior Views for Enhanced Knowledge Grounding
papers.tldr: Regret Pre-training lets one model teach its causal predictions using future-aware training context, improving reported downstream accuracy without adding parameters.

papers.title: Representational Curvature Modulates Behavioral Uncertainty in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: In two language models, contextual representation curvature relates to next-token entropy, and trajectory-aligned interventions can selectively change that uncertainty.

papers.title: Resting Neurons, Active Insights: Robustifying Activation Sparsity in LLMs via Spontaneity
papers.tldr: SPON stabilizes sparsified language models with learned input-independent activation anchors that add negligible inference overhead.

papers.title: Revisiting Anisotropy in Language Transformers: The Geometry of Learning Dynamics
papers.tldr: The paper studies Transformer anisotropy through representation geometry and training-checkpoint analyses linking embedding structure with on-manifold entropy.

papers.title: Shared Semantics, Divergent Mechanisms: Unsupervised Feature Discovery by Aligning Semantics and Mechanisms
papers.tldr: Joint clustering of continuation meanings and mechanistic attributions reveals model behaviors missed by single-view analyses and supports targeted interventions.

papers.title: Spherical Steering: Geometry-Aware Activation Rotation for Language Models
papers.tldr: Spherical Steering rotates hidden activations without changing their magnitude, improving targeted performance while maintaining open-ended generation quality.

papers.title: Steering at the Source: Style Modulation Heads for Robust Persona Control
papers.tldr: Targeting three identified style-related attention heads controls persona while reducing the coherence damage associated with residual-stream steering.

papers.title: Steering Out-of-Distribution Generalization with Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning
papers.tldr: CAFT ablates undesirable internal concept directions during fine-tuning, reducing reported misaligned responses tenfold without changing training data.

papers.title: Subliminal Effects in Your Data: A General Mechanism via Log-Linearity
papers.tldr: Logit-Linear Selection finds preference-data subsets that induce hidden behavioral changes across different model architectures.

papers.title: Syntax vs. Semantics: How Transformers Learn Deep Dependencies
papers.tldr: The paper links delayed structural reasoning to suppressed semantic gradients and uses that analysis to improve variable-binding training.

papers.title: Task-Awareness Improves LLM Generations and Uncertainty
papers.tldr: Modeling answers in task-specific structures enables better synthesized responses and uncertainty estimates more aligned with correctness.

papers.title: The Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis for Language Model Steering
papers.tldr: The Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis explains steering variability through overlapping concept geometry and sample-specific regions of sensitivity.

papers.title: The Devil is in the Spectrum: Mitigating Representation Collapse in LLMs via Topologically Regularized Side-Path
papers.tldr: TRSP adds a lightweight side path that balances information mixing and representation capacity, improving reported long-context performance.

papers.title: The Expert Strikes Back: Interpreting Mixture-of-Experts Language Models at Expert Level
papers.tldr: MoE experts show less mixed neuron meanings and appear to specialize in fine-grained tasks, making experts useful units for interpretation.

papers.title: The First Drop of Ink: Nonlinear Impact of Distracting Information in Long-Context Reasoning
papers.tldr: A small fraction of hard distractors causes most of the observed long-context reasoning damage, with diminishing harm from additional distractors.

papers.title: The Geometric Origin of Grokking: Accelerating Generalization via Active Structural Reorganization
papers.tldr: The paper links grokking to angular reorganization of token representations and introduces a loss that actively encourages this transition.

papers.title: The Information Geometry of Softmax: Probing and Steering
papers.tldr: Dual steering uses the information geometry of softmax representations to target concepts while minimizing off-target changes.

papers.title: The Mechanistic Emergence of Symbol Grounding in Language Models
papers.tldr: Controlled causal analysis finds emergent symbol grounding concentrated in middle-layer computations across several tested model architectures.

papers.title: The Power of Power Law: Asymmetry Enables Compositional Reasoning
papers.tldr: Power-law training distributions improve compositional reasoning in the studied tasks by letting frequent skill combinations support learning of rarer ones.

papers.title: The Shape of Addition: Geometric Structures of Arithmetic in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper links addition errors to noisy carry-related geometry and uses geometric consistency checks to detect and correct studied failures.

papers.title: The Truth Lies Somewhere in the Middle (of the Generated Tokens)
papers.tldr: Pooling representations across generated tokens provides a more informative summary of model state than selecting any individual token.

papers.title: The Truth Stays in the Family: Enhancing Contextual Truthfulness via Inherited Heads in Model Lineages
papers.tldr: TruthProbe amplifies context-truthful attention heads whose scores persist across model families, improving contextual truthfulness and reducing evaluated multimodal hallucinations.

papers.title: Toward Stable Value Alignment: Introducing Independent Modules for Consistent Value Guidance
papers.tldr: SVGT uses an independent value module and Bridge Tokens to reduce harmful outputs while maintaining fluency in reported evaluations.

papers.title: Towards Atoms of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Atom Theory defines and identifies language-model representation units with near-perfect measured faithfulness and stability.

papers.title: Towards Understanding Steering Strength
papers.tldr: Theory and experiments show that steering strength can affect language-model behavior non-monotonically, making intervention magnitude crucial to effective control.

papers.title: Tracing the Persona Circuit: How Large Language Models Encode and Express Character Traits
papers.tldr: A Latent Persona Vector reveals competition behind character drift and guides a small attention-head intervention that improves persona consistency.

papers.title: Trading Complexity for Expressivity Through Structured Generalized Linear Token Mixing
papers.tldr: A unified token-mixing framework uses structured multi-state recurrences to study and design principled runtime-expressivity trade-offs.

papers.title: Translation Heads: Disentangling meaning from language in LLM-based machine translation
papers.tldr: Distinct sparse attention-head sets support language choice and meaning preservation, enabling targeted steering of sentence translation.

papers.title: Universal One-third Time Scaling in Learning Peaked Distributions
papers.tldr: Softmax and cross-entropy can intrinsically produce one-third power-law loss scaling when learning peaked probability distributions.

papers.title: Unlearning Isn’t Deletion: Investigating Reversibility of Machine Unlearning in LLMs
papers.tldr: Representation-level analysis shows that apparent unlearning can be readily reversible, exposing gaps in evaluations based only on task performance.

papers.title: Unraveling Syntax: Language Modeling and the Substructure of Grammars
papers.tldr: Subgrammar analysis decomposes language-model loss and shows that structural pretraining improves internal alignment more consistently than final performance.
